questions.question: Is the output of this project intended for actual wagering, or for private research only?
questions.known: NBA.com Terms of Use section 9(iv): 'the NBA Statistics may not be used in connection with any gambling activity (including legal gambling activity).' Read on the official page this session (S-10).
questions.missing: The owner's intended use. Everything else depends on it.
questions.discovery: Owner decision, then counsel review before any pick, stake, or odds figure is published.

questions.question: Which jurisdiction and licensing position applies?
questions.known: The workspace is located in Amsterdam, Netherlands. An earlier session read that remote sports betting requires a licence under Art. 31a Wet op de kansspelen (S-13).
questions.missing: Whether the user intends to wager, from which country, and whether any licence is held.
questions.discovery: Legal counsel in the relevant jurisdiction; then encode jurisdiction rules in the site.

questions.question: Do we have licensed market prices (odds), and on what terms?
questions.status: BLOCKING for any EV / ROI / closing-line claim
questions.known: None. This repository contains no odds feed, no price snapshots, and no licence.
questions.missing: Provider, markets covered, timestamp granularity, historical depth, permitted display and derivative use, cost.
questions.discovery: Procure provider documentation and written rights; run a coverage and latency audit before any economic test.

questions.question: What is the objective function and the risk policy?
questions.known: The brief asks for a leaderboard that rewards top-performing, skill-based strategies.
questions.missing: Primary metric (Brier / log loss, calibration, or net return), bankroll, stake sizing, drawdown cap, responsible-gambling limits.
questions.discovery: Pre-register the metric and the risk policy before looking at further results.

questions.question: How much authorised history do we have?
questions.known: This project holds 174 completed games, 2026-10-20 through 2026-11-12, reconciled to official GP and W-L for all 30 teams.
questions.missing: Prior seasons, play-by-play, lineups, and possession-level data.
questions.discovery: Inventory authorised sources, then extend the archive with immutable dated snapshots.

questions.question: Do we have per-player game logs?
questions.status: BLOCKING for player correlations and prop distributions
questions.known: No. Only season-to-date averages for the top 31 players by minutes are held (S-09).
questions.missing: Player-level game logs (about 4,000 rows for the season to date).
questions.discovery: Capture nba.com/stats/players/boxscores by date, if permitted under the terms decision in Q-01.

questions.question: What proves a strategy is skill rather than luck?
questions.known: Seven gates are implemented (G1 provenance, G2 no look-ahead, G3 n>=100, G4 power, G5 raw p<0.05, G6 Benjamini-Hochberg FDR 0.05, G7 split-half stability). Zero of eight candidate strategies pass all of them.
questions.missing: Owner approval of the thresholds and of the 100-bet minimum.
questions.discovery: Approve or amend the gate definitions in writing, then re-run.

questions.question: Is the totals model usable at all?
questions.known: Walk-forward over 114 out-of-sample games: totals RMSE 20.35 against a 19.56 naive baseline. The model is worse than the baseline. Margin RMSE 16.18 against a 17.30 baseline.
questions.missing: A totals estimator that beats the naive baseline.
questions.discovery: Add pace/opponent-adjusted estimators and re-test walk-forward; do not publish totals bets until then.

questions.question: What is the prediction cut-off and refresh cadence?
questions.known: The site publishes up to three days ahead (D+1 to D+3). Teams must file by 5pm local the day before a game, so injury data for D+2 and D+3 does not exist yet at publication time (S-01).
questions.missing: A fixed cut-off time, a staleness rule, and a suppression rule when inputs are stale.
questions.discovery: Define UTC timestamps and suppression rules; do not publish a pick on stale inputs.

questions.question: What are the settlement rules?
questions.known: None recorded. Overtime is handled in this project by including OT scoring in the game total (9 of 174 games went to overtime, 5.2%).
questions.missing: Whether a bet settles on regulation or including OT; void/push rules; player-prop rules when a player does not appear.
questions.discovery: Obtain the rule book of whichever venue is used, and record it before scoring anything.

questions.question: How dependent are the legs of a same-game parlay?
questions.known: Spread-residual vs total-residual correlation r = +0.091, 95% CI [-0.094, +0.270], n = 114 out-of-sample. Joint hit rate 0.246 against 0.219 under independence.
questions.missing: A sample large enough to separate +0.09 from zero, and any player-level dependence measure at all.
questions.discovery: Extend the sample; capture player game logs (Q-06); report intervals, not point values.

questions.question: Who owns model versioning, promotion, and retirement?
questions.known: No model registry exists. The current build is reproducible by re-running final/build_model.py.
questions.missing: Versioning, promotion criteria, drift monitoring, and a retirement rule.
questions.discovery: Create a model register with frozen versions before any strategy is promoted.

questions.question: May this data be published on a public web page at all?
questions.known: Terms section 1 permits personal, non-commercial use only; section 9(ii) permits legitimate news reporting or private non-commercial use; section 9(vii) restricts a comprehensive, regularly updated statistics database without express prior consent (S-10).
questions.missing: Written permission from the NBA, or a licensed commercial data feed.
questions.discovery: Seek written consent or switch to a licensed provider. Until then treat this site as internal research.

questions.question: Should the six session dashboards be consolidated or kept?
questions.known: docs/ (23 files), site/ (29), edge/ (25), lab/ (17), origin/ (22), research/ (16) each publish a separate dashboard with its own ID scheme, plus a seventh root dashboard.
questions.missing: The owner's preference: consolidate into one site and archive the rest, or maintain all seven.
questions.discovery: Choose an option on the Suggestions page (SG-08).

questions.question: Why is data/raw sourced from a non-official site?
questions.known: data/raw/results_2026-27_october.csv and _november.csv carry a header stating Basketball-Reference as their source.
questions.missing: Whether that source is permitted, and whether it was reconciled to an official source.
questions.discovery: Either reconcile those files to nba.com or remove them. The consolidated dataset does not use them.

suggestions.suggestion: Decide, in writing, whether NBA data may be used for this purpose at all.
suggestions.why: Terms section 9(iv) bars use of NBA Statistics in connection with any gambling activity, including legal gambling activity. Every other decision is downstream of this one.
suggestions.options: A. Private research only - keep the site private, publish no picks. B. Obtain the NBA's express written consent. C. Replace NBA data with a licensed commercial feed that grants the needed rights.
suggestions.recommended: A now; evaluate B or C only if wagering is intended.

suggestions.suggestion: Procure a licensed odds feed before any economic claim is made.
suggestions.why: Without timestamped prices there is no way to compute expected value, closing-line value, or return. Everything economic on this site is therefore blank.
suggestions.options: A. No feed - score on self-consistency and proper scoring rules only. B. Free/low-cost snapshot capture with manual timestamping. C. Paid provider with historical depth and written rights.
suggestions.recommended: A for now, C if the project moves to live scoring.

suggestions.suggestion: Capture per-player game logs by date.
suggestions.why: Player-level correlations, prop distributions, and the injury-to-production chain are all blocked without them. Three of seven correlation rows are blank for exactly this reason.
suggestions.options: A. Capture nba.com/stats/players/boxscores by date (about 4,000 rows for the season to date). B. Licensed provider. C. Leave blank and do not publish player markets.
suggestions.recommended: C until Q-01 is settled, then A or B.

suggestions.suggestion: Capture the full official player minutes table, not only the top 31.
suggestions.why: Every minutes-vacuum figure is currently a floor: an injured player outside the top 31 contributes zero measured minutes. The official table has about 465 rows.
suggestions.options: A. Capture all pages of the official table. B. Capture the top 100 only. C. Keep the top 31 and label all vacuum figures as floors.
suggestions.recommended: A; C is the current state and is flagged (F-12).

suggestions.suggestion: Do not publish totals bets until a totals model beats the naive baseline.
suggestions.why: The walk-forward totals RMSE is 20.35 against a 19.56 baseline. The margin model beats its baseline (16.18 vs 17.30) but explains only 12.5% of margin variance.
suggestions.options: A. Publish margins only. B. Add pace and opponent-adjusted estimators and re-test. C. Publish both and disclose the failure.
suggestions.recommended: B, with A in the meantime.

suggestions.suggestion: Approve the seven validation gates and the 100-bet minimum, or replace them.
suggestions.why: The gates are proposed, not approved. Zero of eight strategies pass, so the thresholds determine the entire leaderboard.
suggestions.options: A. Approve as-is (n>=100, p<0.05, BH-FDR 0.05, split-half stability). B. Lower the sample floor and accept provisional status with disclosure. C. Replace with a proper-scoring-rule leaderboard (Brier / log loss) plus calibration.
suggestions.recommended: C plus A: score calibration first, then admit a strategy to a return leaderboard only after the sample gate.

suggestions.suggestion: Automate injury-report capture on a schedule and keep every revision.
suggestions.why: Reports are published 15 minutes apart all day and are overwritten in place at the index. Right now the capture is manual, so D+2 and D+3 slates have no injury data at all.
suggestions.options: A. Scheduled job capturing every report and storing each PDF revision. B. Capture only the 5pm and 1pm deadlines. C. Keep manual capture.
suggestions.recommended: B as a first step, A as the target.

suggestions.suggestion: Consolidate the seven overlapping dashboards into one.
suggestions.why: docs/, site/, edge/, lab/, origin/, research/ and d01ae7e2/ publish similar tables with different ID schemes, and five later unified builds (/ + /app/, /dash/, /hub/, /d01ae7e2/, /dashboard/) each present themselves as the answer. That is the single biggest source of confusion on the live site.
suggestions.options: A. One canonical dashboard; move the six session directories under /archive/ and link them from one page. B. Keep all seven and add a clear landing page that explains each. C. Delete the superseded ones.
suggestions.recommended: A. This session built the consolidated dashboard at the site root and left the six session directories in place, linked from the Archives page.
suggestions.recommendation: **A. This session did NOT consolidate the site root** — it published its verified build under /dashboard/ instead, because sessions a459dadf (/ + /app/) and 2b9f1ae1 (/dash/) already own their trees and 99eabb04 (/hub/) and d01ae7e2 joined meanwhile. Deleting any of them is an owner decision, not a session decision. See CR-925439ca-E.

suggestions.suggestion: Pick one GitHub Pages deployment mechanism.
suggestions.why: Two are active: the legacy 'main /' branch build and the Actions workflow artifact. They currently serve the same tree, but they can diverge silently.
suggestions.options: A. Switch Pages to the GitHub Actions source and delete the legacy build. B. Keep the legacy build and drop the workflow deploy job. C. Leave both and add a parity check.
suggestions.recommended: A. Earlier sessions could not change the setting (HTTP 403); the change needs a repository owner.

suggestions.suggestion: Add a LICENSE file and a Python project manifest.
suggestions.why: The repository has no LICENSE (so default copyright applies) and no pyproject.toml. requirements.txt pins only requests==2.31.0, which the current pipeline does not import.
suggestions.options: A. Add MIT or Apache-2.0 plus a pyproject.toml. B. Add LICENSE only. C. Leave as is.

suggestions.suggestion: Remove or reconcile the non-official data files in data/raw/.
suggestions.why: Those CSVs are headed 'source: Basketball-Reference'. Every other table on this site is reconciled to an official NBA page, so they are inconsistent with the verification policy.
suggestions.options: A. Reconcile them to nba.com and record the check. B. Delete them. C. Move them to /archive/.
suggestions.recommended: A if they are still used, otherwise B.

suggestions.suggestion: Create a model register with frozen versions before promoting any strategy.
suggestions.why: No versioning, promotion criteria, drift monitoring, or retirement rule exists. A leaderboard without them invites post-hoc selection.
suggestions.options: A. Register with semantic versions, promotion checklist, and a retirement rule. B. Git tags only. C. Nothing yet.
suggestions.recommended: A before any strategy is called deployable.

suggestions.suggestion: Define a fixed prediction cut-off, staleness rule, and suppression rule.
suggestions.why: Injury reports arrive up to tip-off. Without a rule, a published line can silently rest on stale availability data - and five of ten team reports for the D+1 slate were still 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' at capture.
suggestions.options: A. Cut off at the 5pm local filing deadline; suppress any game with a missing report. B. Cut off 2 hours before tip; show a staleness badge. C. Publish regardless and show the capture timestamp.
suggestions.recommended: A plus a visible capture timestamp.

suggestions.suggestion: Record settlement rules before scoring any result.
suggestions.why: Overtime, pushes, and prop voids change results. Nine of 174 games went to overtime this season, so the OT convention alone moves outcomes.
suggestions.options: A. Record the venue rule book and encode it. B. Assume regulation-only and disclose. C. Assume including OT and disclose.
suggestions.recommended: A. The model currently uses totals including OT, which is disclosed.

flags.title: NBA Terms of Use section 9(iv) bars use of NBA Statistics in connection with gambling
flags.detail: Verbatim from the official page: 'the NBA Statistics may not be used in connection with any gambling activity (including legal gambling activity)'. Read this session.
flags.effect: No pick, stake, or odds figure derived from NBA Statistics may be published for gambling use until this is resolved.

flags.title: Terms section 9(vii) restricts a comprehensive regularly updated statistics database
flags.detail: Verbatim: NBA Statistics may not be used in connection with any website, product, or service that features a database of comprehensive, regularly updated statistics from NBA games 'without the Operator's express prior consent'.
flags.effect: This repository is exactly such a database. Publishing it publicly needs express consent or a licensed feed.

flags.title: No licensed market prices
flags.detail: The repository contains no odds feed, no price snapshots, and no licence.
flags.effect: Every expected-value, return-on-investment, and closing-line figure on this site is blank by policy. Nothing economic can be claimed.

flags.title: No per-player game logs
flags.detail: Only season-to-date averages for the top 31 players by minutes are held.
flags.effect: Three of seven correlation rows are blank, and no player-prop distribution is established. All player projections on this site are point estimates from season averages and are labelled unverified.

flags.title: Injury coverage is incomplete for the published slate
flags.detail: The newest official report at capture (11/13/26 07:30 PM ET) covers the 11/13 games and the 11/14 slate only. For 11/14, five of ten team reports read 'NOT YET SUBMITTED' (NOP, CLE, MEM, CHI, MIA). No 11/15 or 11/16 report exists yet: teams file by 5pm local the day before a game.
flags.effect: Availability inputs for 11/15 and 11/16 are absent, not zero. Lines for those dates carry no injury adjustment.

flags.title: The 2025-26 injury index URL serves 2026-27 content
flags.detail: https://official.nba.com/nba-injury-report-2025-26-season/ resolves and returns a page titled 'NBA Injury Report: 2026-27 Season' listing 11/13/2026 reports.
flags.effect: An earlier dashboard cited that URL as the 2025-26 report. It must not be cited as such.

flags.title: Injury PDF uses merged cells, so 60 of 122 rows inherit team and matchup
flags.detail: The PDF prints game date, game time, matchup and team once per group. Rows below the first in a group show those cells blank. They were filled forward from the printed value immediately above, inside the same official PDF, and every such row is marked 'inherited' on the Injuries page.
flags.effect: Attribution is correct only if no page break splits a group mid-way. Rows are marked so a reviewer can audit them.

flags.title: PDF text extraction concatenates words across line breaks
flags.detail: The extracted text contains strings such as 'Right High AnkleSprain', 'Left Knee InjuryManagement' and 'Left Ankle InjuryRecovery'. A single space was inserted where the PDF wraps mid-word during transcription.
flags.effect: Reason strings on this site are whitespace-normalised relative to the raw extraction. The underlying words are unchanged.

flags.title: The totals model is worse than a naive baseline
flags.detail: Walk-forward, 114 out-of-sample games: totals RMSE 20.35 against a 19.56 naive baseline (variance explained -8.2%). Margin RMSE 16.18 against a 17.30 baseline (variance explained +12.5%).
flags.effect: Totals lines are published as research output with the failure disclosed. They are not a validated edge.

flags.title: Fitted home-court advantage is not statistically significant
flags.detail: Least-squares fit over 173 non-neutral games: +1.59 points, two-sided p = 0.104, df = 172. Mean home margin is +1.70 points.
flags.effect: The value is used in the model but should not be quoted as an established effect at this sample size.

flags.title: Zero of eight candidate strategies pass all seven gates
flags.detail: Two are provisional: S5 (fade originated totals of 235+) is 21/24, p = 0.0003, survives FDR, split-half stable, but needs n >= 56 for 80% power and the gate floor is 100. S4b (back road favourites of 8+) is 20/28, p = 0.036, does not survive FDR.
flags.effect: Nothing is deployable. The leaderboard is empty by design.

flags.title: Only the top 31 players by minutes are captured
flags.detail: The official player table has about 465 rows; this project holds ranks 1-31.
flags.effect: Every minutes-vacuum figure is a floor. An injured player outside the top 31 contributes zero measured minutes to the estimate.

flags.title: Eleven overlapping dashboards on one Pages site, five of them unified
flags.detail: docs/ (23 files), site/ (29), edge/ (25), lab/ (17), origin/ (22), research/ (16) and d01ae7e2/ publish similar tables with different ID schemes. Five later builds each present themselves as the single answer: / + /app/ (session a459dadf), /dash/ (2b9f1ae1 / e40cd215), /hub/ (99eabb04), /d01ae7e2/ (d01ae7e2) and /dashboard/ (this session, 925439ca). This build is published under /dashboard/ precisely so it does not overwrite the site root, which another session owns.
flags.effect: Reviewers cannot tell which numbers are canonical. Naming one canonical dashboard is an owner decision, not a session decision — see SG-08 and change request CR-925439ca-E in COORDINATION.md. Nothing on this site claims to supersede the others.

flags.title: Two GitHub Pages deployment mechanisms are active
flags.detail: Pages is configured with the legacy 'main /' branch build, and a workflow also uploads and deploys an artifact. They currently serve the same tree.
flags.effect: They can diverge silently. Switching to the Actions source returned HTTP 403 for earlier sessions.

flags.title: Data runs through 2026-11-12; nine 11/13 games were in progress at capture
flags.detail: The official games page for 11/13 showed games in Q2 and at the end of Q1 at retrieval time (about 18:40 ET).
flags.effect: The 174-game log stops at 11/12. Lines for 11/14 onward are fitted on it. Re-running final/build_model.py after 11/13 games finish will extend it.

flags.title: Competition, venue and city are blank for the published slate
flags.detail: The official games pages do not print the competition/round for the 11/14-11/16 games, and no venue source was captured.
flags.effect: Those columns are left blank and flagged rather than filled in.

flags.title: Player-prop projections are point estimates, not distributions
flags.detail: Projections scale a player's official season averages by a projected-minutes multiple. The minutes redistribution itself uses an unverified pro-rata assumption and no per-player game logs.
flags.effect: No over/under probability for any player market is established. Every projection row is labelled unverified.

flags.title: Overtime probability is a league base rate, not a game-specific estimate
flags.detail: Every line carries p(OT) = 0.0517, the observed rate of 9 overtime games in 174. No game-specific OT model was fitted.
flags.effect: Treat it as a league average, not a forecast for a particular game.

flags.title: Per-PR CI checks are invisible: the GitHub connection is an integration token
flags.detail: Branch pushes from this workspace create zero workflow runs (actions/runs?branch=arena/925439ca-nba3 returns total_count: 0) and dispatching a workflow manually fails with HTTP 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'. Merges to main do trigger the push workflow, so the post-merge run exists and was green (run 43540337304).
flags.effect: PR #34 shows no check runs in its own UI. Every check was run locally on the exact rebased tree before merging, and the same checks ran green on main afterwards. A reviewer using a user token would see per-PR checks normally.
